-zsh.summary: A login shell. The leading dash is how Unix marks a shell started as the first process of a terminal session (zsh, macOS's default shell).
-zsh.why: A Terminal, iTerm2 or similar window (or an app that opens a terminal, such as an IDE or Claude Code) started it.
-zsh.quit: Closing that terminal tab ends it; anything running inside it stops too.

pidwick.summary: This app: the process viewer you are looking at.

1Password.why: Installed from 1password.com or the App Store; usually set to launch at login.
1Password.quit: Quit like any app. This locks your vault and stops autofill until you reopen it.

1Password-BrowserSupport.summary: The bridge between 1Password's browser extension and the 1Password desktop app. Chrome, Firefox, Safari and others talk to it to unlock and autofill.
1Password-BrowserSupport.why: Started by the browser extension (native messaging) when you use 1Password in a browser.
1Password-BrowserSupport.quit: Safe: it ends when the browser closes or when it is idle; the extension restarts it.

1Password-Crash-Handler.summary: The crash reporter for 1Password. It only does work if 1Password crashes.
1Password-Crash-Handler.quit: Safe, but it quits with 1Password anyway.

2BUA8C4S2C.com.1password.browser-helper.summary: The 1Password Safari-extension helper. The leading code is 1Password's Apple Team ID (2BUA8C4S2C).
2BUA8C4S2C.com.1password.browser-helper.why: Started by the 1Password for Safari extension.
2BUA8C4S2C.com.1password.browser-helper.quit: Safe; it restarts when Safari needs it.

ChatGPT for Chrome.summary: A native-messaging host from OpenAI's Codex plugin. It connects the Codex/ChatGPT Chrome extension with the Codex app on your Mac so Codex can see and drive Chrome tabs.
ChatGPT for Chrome.why: Installed with the Codex Chrome plugin (look in ~/.codex/plugins). Chrome starts it when the extension connects.
ChatGPT for Chrome.quit: Safe; disconnecting it just stops Codex's browser control until Chrome starts it again.

chrome-native-host.summary: The native-messaging host that connects the Claude in Chrome browser extension with the Claude desktop app.
chrome-native-host.why: Installed with Claude.app. Chrome launches it when the Claude extension is active.
chrome-native-host.quit: Safe; the extension relaunches it when needed.

chrome_crashpad_handler.summary: Chromium's crash reporter. Chrome and Chromium-based apps (Electron apps, Edge, Brave) launch one to collect crash dumps.
chrome_crashpad_handler.why: Starts with the app that uses Chromium.
chrome_crashpad_handler.quit: Ends with its app. Safe to ignore.

Google Chrome.summary: The Chrome web browser's main (browser) process.
Google Chrome.why: You or an extension/app opened Chrome.
Google Chrome.quit: Quit like any app. Its many 'Helper' processes close with it.

Code.summary: The main process of Visual Studio Code (or a similar Electron editor).
Code.quit: Quit like any app (save your files first). Its Helper, extension host and language-server child processes close with it.

Lunar.summary: Lunar: an app that controls the brightness, volume and inputs of external displays (using DDC) and keeps them in sync with the built-in screen.
Lunar.why: Installed by you; usually runs at login in the menu bar.
Lunar.quit: Quit from its menu-bar item. Your displays keep their last brightness but stop auto-adjusting.

Dropbox.summary: The Dropbox desktop app. It syncs your Dropbox folder and shows a menu-bar item.
Dropbox.why: Installed by you; set to open at login.
Dropbox.quit: Quit from its menu. Syncing stops until you reopen it.

DropboxFileProvider.summary: Dropbox's File Provider extension. It is how Dropbox files appear in Finder's sidebar as an online-only/synced folder.
DropboxFileProvider.why: Part of Dropbox; loaded by macOS's fileproviderd.
DropboxFileProvider.quit: Leave it; macOS restarts it. Quit Dropbox to stop it.

DropboxFileProviderCH.summary: A helper of Dropbox's File Provider extension that handles content-heavy work such as downloads.
DropboxFileProviderCH.quit: Leave it; quit Dropbox to stop it.

ShipIt.summary: Squirrel.Mac's updater ('ShipIt'). Many Electron apps (Slack, Discord, Notion, Atom, GitHub Desktop) use it to download and install their own updates.
ShipIt.why: Runs after an app such as Slack finds an update or at its next restart.
ShipIt.quit: Safe; if an update was mid-install, restart the app to retry.

Notion.why: You opened Notion; many Notion helpers appear alongside it.

Slack.summary: The Slack desktop app (an Electron app).
Slack.why: You opened Slack; usually launched at login.
Slack.quit: Quit like any app. Its Helper processes close with it.

iTerm2.quit: Quit like any app; running sessions will end unless you use tmux/session restoration.

pidinfo.summary: An iTerm2 helper (XPC service) that looks up information about running processes, such as which job is in the foreground, for the status bar and Triggers.
pidinfo.why: Bundled inside iTerm2; started by iTerm2.

claude.summary: Claude Code, Anthropic's command-line AI coding agent. It reads your project, edits files and runs commands on your behalf.
claude.why: You (or an IDE integration) ran `claude` in a terminal.
claude.quit: Press Ctrl-C twice in its terminal, or close it. Stopping it halts any work in progress.

codex.summary: OpenAI Codex: a coding agent. This process is Codex's local app-server that the Codex app and its extensions talk to.
codex.quit: Quitting the Codex app ends it. Killing it stops any running Codex tasks.

opencode.summary: opencode: an open-source AI coding agent for the terminal.
opencode.quit: Close the terminal session or press Ctrl-C.

copilot-runtime.summary: The runtime behind GitHub Copilot's agent features inside VS Code.
copilot-runtime.why: Launched by the GitHub Copilot extension in VS Code.
copilot-runtime.quit: Safe; VS Code restarts it when you use Copilot.

clojure-lsp.summary: A Clojure language server. Editors use it for completion, navigation and linting.
clojure-lsp.why: Started by the Calva extension (or another Clojure editor plug-in).

cloudflared.summary: Cloudflare's tunnel daemon. It creates an outbound encrypted tunnel so a local service can be reached through Cloudflare without opening a port.
cloudflared.why: You (or a Homebrew service) ran `cloudflared`, often for a Cloudflare Tunnel.
cloudflared.quit: Stopping it closes the tunnel. Check what it exposes before stopping or leaving it on.

java.summary: A Java Virtual Machine running a Java (or Clojure/Kotlin/Scala) program. The arguments show which program.
java.why: A Java application, build tool or language server was started.
java.quit: Depends on what it runs; see the command line before killing it.

mosquitto.summary: Eclipse Mosquitto: an MQTT message broker used by smart-home and IoT systems. It listens for network connections.
mosquitto.why: Installed with Homebrew and usually started as a service.
mosquitto.quit: Stopping it disconnects devices that publish to it (Home Assistant sensors, etc.). Check if you rely on it.

gitstatusd-darwin-arm64.summary: gitstatus: a fast git status daemon used by the Powerlevel10k zsh prompt to show branch and change info instantly.
gitstatusd-darwin-arm64.why: Started by your zsh theme (Powerlevel10k) for each shell.
gitstatusd-darwin-arm64.quit: Safe; it exits when the shell does.

go.summary: The Go toolchain (go build, go run, go test…).
go.why: You or a tool ran a Go command.
go.quit: Safe; it ends the running build/command.

proc.test.summary: A compiled Go test binary (named after the package under test) started by `go test`.
proc.test.why: You or a tool ran `go test`.
proc.test.quit: Safe; it ends the test run.

ps.summary: The `ps` command listing processes. Pidwick itself runs it to refresh its list.
ps.why: Pidwick, a script, or you ran it.

caffeinate.summary: Keeps the Mac awake (stops sleep) while it runs.
caffeinate.why: You or a program ran `caffeinate`, for example to stop sleep during a long job.
caffeinate.quit: Safe; stopping it lets the Mac sleep again.

ssh-agent.summary: Holds your decrypted SSH keys in memory so you don't retype passphrases.
ssh-agent.why: Started by macOS at login (or by your shell).
ssh-agent.quit: Safe; you will be asked for key passphrases again.

RTProtectionDaemon.summary: Malwarebytes' real-time protection daemon. It scans files and processes for malware as they are used. Reports exist of it using a lot of CPU.
RTProtectionDaemon.why: Runs if Malwarebytes for Mac is installed and protection is on.
RTProtectionDaemon.quit: Quit Malwarebytes protection from its app. Force-killing it just makes it restart.

mbuseragent.summary: Malwarebytes' per-user agent: shows its notifications and menu-bar item.

SettingsDaemon.summary: Malwarebytes' settings daemon: keeps its configuration, subscription status and policies.

FrontendAgent.summary: Malwarebytes' agent that connects its background engine with the user interface.

com.malwarebytes.mbam.engine.sys.ext.summary: Malwarebytes' system extension (Endpoint Security). It lets Malwarebytes watch process and file activity system-wide.
com.malwarebytes.mbam.engine.sys.ext.why: Approved in System Settings > Privacy & Security when you installed Malwarebytes.
com.malwarebytes.mbam.engine.sys.ext.quit: Don't kill; remove it through Malwarebytes' uninstaller.

com.microsoft.teams2.agent.summary: A login-item agent that belongs to the new Microsoft Teams app. It keeps notifications and presence running.
com.microsoft.teams2.agent.quit: Quit Teams or turn off 'Open at login' in its settings.
